name: Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Temple, Annavaram
nativeName: శ్రీ వీర వేంకట సత్యనారాయణ స్వామి ఆలయం, అన్నవరం
deity: Vishnu as Sri Satyanarayana Swamy, with Anantalakshmi, on the Ratnagiri hill
period: A hill shrine of Satyanarayana on the Pampa, sought above all for the Satyanarayana Vratam
dynasty: Local patronage; the present temple raised in modern times
summary: On the Ratnagiri hill above the Pampa river, Vishnu is worshipped as Satyanarayana with Anantalakshmi — the great home of the Satyanarayana Vratam, the vow of truth kept in countless Telugu households.

sections.history: Annavaram crowns the Ratnagiri hill by the Pampa river in the Godavari country of Andhra Pradesh. Here Vishnu is worshipped as Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana, the lord of truth, with his consort Anantalakshmi; it is among the most visited temples of coastal Andhra, sought above all by families keeping the Satyanarayana Vratam.
sections.architecture: The temple stands atop the hill in the Dravidian manner, its main shrine laid out as a cosmic diagram — a two-tiered structure with the presiding deity above and the Yantra of worship below, echoing the form of a great mandala. The hill is reached by road and by steps, with the Pampa winding below.
sections.legends: Satyanarayana is the form of Vishnu whose story is read at the Vratam — the vow by which a family, rich or poor, honours the lord of truth with a simple offering and the reading of his tale. The temple is held to grant the fruit of this vow, and pilgrims come to perform it before the god himself.
sections.festivals: Every day sees families performing the Satyanarayana Vratam, and full-moon days and Kalyanotsavam draw the greatest crowds. The god's own wedding festival and the Prabhala and hill festivals fill the year.
sections.experience: Annavaram is a temple of the household vow made pilgrimage — to climb the Ratnagiri and keep the Satyanarayana Vratam before the lord is, for many Telugu families, a once-in-a-lifetime fulfilment.

visit.timings: Open daily from early morning to night with darshan and Vratam sessions; full-moon days and Kalyanotsavam are busiest, and the Vratam is best booked ahead. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Annavaram lies in Kakinada district of Andhra Pradesh, on the Chennai–Howrah route; it has its own railway station, and the hilltop is reached by road and by steps.
